rules.summary: A provider may bill the survivor's insurer for a sexual assault exam only if the survivor authorizes it, and may ask for that authorization only after the exam.
rules.quote: The hospital or other licensed health care provider performing the examination may seek insurance reimbursement from the victim's insurer only if authorized by the victim. This authorization may only be sought after the examination is performed.

rules.summary: When asking for that consent, the provider must tell the survivor that the state is required to pay and that the survivor owes nothing and does not have to authorize insurance billing.
rules.quote: the state is required by law to pay for the examination and that the victim is in no way liable for these costs or obligated to authorize the reimbursement

params.payer: State of Minnesota; providers submit exam costs to the Department of Public Safety Office of Justice Programs

rules.summary: The state pays for the exam of a victim of criminal sexual conduct that occurred in Minnesota, including STI tests and treatment and emergency contraception. Providers send the costs to the Office of Justice Programs.
rules.quote: for the examination of a victim of criminal sexual conduct that occurred in the state shall be paid by the state. These costs include, but are not limited to, the cost of the medical forensic examination, associated tests and treatments relating to sexually transmitted infection, and pregnancy status, including emergency contraception. A hospital, emergency medical facility, or health care provider shall submit the costs for examination and any associated tests and treatment to the Office of Justice Programs for payment.

rules.summary: State payment for the exam does not depend on reporting to police or on any investigation or prosecution.
rules.quote: The applicability of this section does not depend upon whether the victim reports the offense to law enforcement or the existence or status of any investigation or prosecution.

rules.summary: Reimbursement to all claimants for one victim's injury or death may not exceed $50,000.
rules.quote: reimbursement paid to all claimants suffering economic loss as the result of the injury or death of any one victim shall not exceed $50,000.

rules.summary: The program's own staff training slides list a $7,500 limit for counseling with a licensed provider. The board sets this amount itself, so it can change.
rules.quote: Counseling with licensed provider$7,500

rules.summary: Psychological and psychiatric care needed for the victim's recovery counts as economic loss, up to an amount the board sets.
rules.quote: reasonable expenses incurred for psychological or psychiatric products, services, or accommodations, not to exceed an amount to be set by the board

rules.summary: Lost income is usually paid for up to 26 weeks, with a possible extension of up to 26 more weeks if a physician documents continuing disability.
rules.quote: Compensation for loss of income usually may not exceed 26 weeks. If the victim's disability continues past 26 weeks, the victim may request an extension for up to 26 additional weeks.

rules.summary: The board does not pay for more than 40 missed hours per week.
rules.quote: The board may not compensate for hours missed in excess of 40 hours per week.

rules.summary: Moving expenses, storage fees, and phone and utility installation fees are covered up to $1,000 per claim when the move is needed because of a reasonable fear of danger related to the crime.
rules.quote: the claimant's moving expenses, storage fees, and phone and utility installation fees, up to a maximum of $1,000 per claim, if the move is necessary due to a reasonable fear of danger related to the crime for which the claim was filed

rules.summary: The program's own staff training slides list crime scene cleanup with a $10,000 limit.
rules.quote: scene clean up - $10,000

rules.summary: Child care from a provider exempt from licensing is paid at no more than $3 an hour per child for daytime care or $4 an hour per child for evening care. Licensed facilities are paid up to their standard rate.
rules.quote: Licensed facilities must be paid at a rate not to exceed their standard rate of payment. Facilities exempted from licensing requirements must be paid at a rate not to exceed $3 an hour per child for daytime child care or $4 an hour per child for evening child care

rules.summary: The program's own staff training slides list a $1,500 limit for alternative healing methods such as cultural or religious healing services. The board sets this amount itself, so it can change.
rules.quote: Alternative Healing Methods - $1,500

rules.summary: Necessary medical, hospital, dental, and related expenses, including ambulance and drugs, count as economic loss.
rules.quote: reasonable expenses incurred for necessary medical, chiropractic, hospital, rehabilitative, and dental products, services, or accommodations, including ambulance services, drugs, appliances, and prosthetic devices

rules.summary: Counseling by a licensed provider is covered for victims and their family members.
rules.quote: Counseling expenses by a licensed provider for victims and their family members

rules.summary: Income the victim would have earned had they not been injured counts as economic loss.
rules.quote: loss of income that the victim would have earned had the victim not been injured

rules.summary: Mileage to crime-related medical and counseling appointments is reimbursed at the federal mileage rate.
rules.quote: The reparations program reimburses mileage to medical and counseling appointments that are related to the injury from the crime. Miles are calculated from your home address to the clinic/hospital address and are paid at the current federal mileage rate.

rules.summary: Substitute child care or household services the victim would have provided count as economic loss.
rules.quote: reasonable expenses incurred for substitute child care or household services to replace those the victim or claimant would have performed had the victim or the claimant's child not been injured

params.item: stolen money, property loss, and pain and suffering

rules.summary: Pain and suffering, stolen money, and property loss are not covered.
rules.quote: Pain and suffering, stolen money and property loss are not covered.

rules.summary: Damaged or stolen property is not covered.
rules.quote: Expenses for damaged/stolen property are not covered.

rules.summary: The program's own staff training slides list security systems as not covered.
rules.quote: Non-Covered Expenses Pain and suffering  Property Loss /stolen money Security systems

rules.summary: The program's own staff training slides list clothing and bedding taken as evidence as not covered.
rules.quote: Non-Covered Expenses Pain and suffering  Property Loss /stolen money Security systems  Clothing /Bedding taken as evidence

rules.summary: The program's own staff training slides list attorney's fees as not covered.
rules.quote: Non-Covered Expenses Pain and suffering  Property Loss /stolen money Security systems  Clothing /Bedding taken as evidence Attorney's fees

rules.summary: The board does not reimburse lost tuition, scholarship, or student loan funds, or income lost from delayed schooling.
rules.quote: The board must not reimburse a claimant for loss of tuition, scholarship, or student loan funds or loss of income due to a delay in completion of schooling related to the crime.

params.item: lost wages already covered by sick leave, vacation, compensatory time, or holiday pay

rules.summary: Wages already covered by the claimant's paid leave are not paid.
rules.quote: The board must not pay for lost wages covered by a claimant's accumulated sick leave, vacation leave, compensatory time, or holiday pay.

params.extension: If the claimant was unable to file, three years from when a claim could have been filed; if the injury was not reasonably discoverable, three years from when it became reasonably discoverable.

rules.summary: A claim must be filed within three years of the victim's injury, with extensions when the claimant was unable to file or the injury was not reasonably discoverable.
rules.quote: no claim was filed with the board within three years of victim's injury or death; except that (i) if the claimant was unable to file a claim within that period, then the claim can be made within three years of the time when a claim could have been filed; and (ii) if the victim's injury or death was not reasonably discoverable within three years of the injury or death, then the claim can be made within three years of the time when the injury or death is reasonably discoverable.

rules.summary: For victims of child abuse, the police report time limit and the minimum claim amount do not apply, and the three-year filing period starts when the crime is reported to police.
rules.quote: The limitations contained in clauses (1) and (6) do not apply to victims of child abuse. In those cases the three-year limitation period commences running with the report of the crime to the police.

rules.summary: The crime must be reported to police within 30 days, but a victim of criminal sexual conduct who reports later is treated as having been unable to report sooner.
rules.quote: the crime was not reported to the police within 30 days of its occurrence or, if it could not reasonably have been reported within that period, within 30 days of the time when a report could reasonably have been made. A victim of criminal sexual conduct in the first, second, third, or fourth degree who does not report the crime within 30 days of its occurrence is deemed to have been unable to have reported it within that period

rules.summary: The program says there is no time limit to report for sexual assault victims, but the crime must still be reported to police.
rules.quote: Crime must have been reported to police within 30 days (no time limit for sexual assault and child abuse victims, but crime must be reported)

rules.summary: The victim must cooperate fully with police. Cooperation can be shown by police or prosecutor records, or by a signed document from a victim service, counseling, or medical professional involved in the case. This shows cooperation; it does not replace the police report.
rules.quote: Cooperation is determined through law enforcement reports, prosecutor records, or corroboration memorialized in a signed document submitted by a victim service, counseling, or medical professional involved in the case

rules.summary: No award is made if the claim is less than $50; this limit does not apply to child abuse victims.
rules.quote: or (6) the claim is less than $50. The limitations contained in clauses (1) and (6) do not apply to victims of child abuse.

rules.summary: Reimbursement is reduced by what collateral sources such as insurance pay, and the claimant must try those sources first.
rules.quote: reimbursement shall be reduced to the extent that economic loss is recouped from a collateral source or collateral sources. Where compensation is readily available to a claimant from a collateral source, the claimant must take reasonable steps to recoup from the collateral source before claiming reimbursement

rules.summary: Life insurance and voluntary donations or gifts are not counted as collateral sources.
rules.quote: The term does not include a life insurance contract or benefits from any private source provided as a voluntary donation or gift.

rules.summary: The board may deny or reduce an award for contributory misconduct of the victim.
rules.quote: reimbursement shall be denied or reduced to the extent, if any, that the board deems reasonable because of the contributory misconduct of the claimant or of a victim through whom the claimant claims.

rules.summary: The program's own staff training slides say a misconduct reduction may be waived in domestic or sexual assault cases.
rules.quote: May be waived in cases of domestic or sexual assault

rules.summary: The board may grant emergency reimbursement before a final decision when an award is probable and waiting would cause undue hardship.
rules.quote: grant emergency reimbursement pending the final determination of a claim if it is one with respect to which an award will probably be made and undue hardship will result to the claimant if immediate payment is not made

rules.summary: Sexual assault is a covered crime.
rules.quote: Homicide Assault Domestic Abuse Sexual Assault Child Abuse (Physical and Sexual)
rules.pinpoint: Financial Help brochure (9/24), types of crimes covered

rules.summary: Injury includes bodily harm, pregnancy, and emotional trauma.
rules.quote: "Injury" means actual bodily harm including pregnancy and emotional trauma.

params.rule: Any victim of a crime in Minnesota may apply; residency and citizenship are not required.

rules.summary: The crime must have occurred in Minnesota; residency and citizenship are not required.
rules.quote: Crime must have occurred in Minnesota (residency/citizenship not required)

params.rule: Minnesota residents victimized outside the state may apply if the place of the crime has no crime victims reimbursement law covering the injury.

rules.summary: A Minnesota resident hurt outside the state can apply if that place has no victim compensation law covering the injury.
rules.quote: A Minnesota resident who is the victim of a crime committed outside the geographical boundaries of this state but who otherwise meets the requirements of this section shall have the same rights under this chapter as if the crime had occurred within this state upon a showing that the state, territory, United States possession, country, or political subdivision of a country in which the crime occurred does not have a crime victims reimbursement law covering the resident's injury or death.

params.rule: The crime must occur or be attempted within Minnesota, including Indian reservations and other trust lands.

rules.summary: By statute, a covered crime is one that occurs or is attempted within Minnesota, including Indian reservations and other trust lands.
rules.quote: occurs or is attempted anywhere within the geographical boundaries of this state, including Indian reservations and other trust lands

params.enroll: If you are eligible, you can enroll in the Safe at Home Program with the help of an Application Assistant.

rules.summary: Safe at Home, run by the Minnesota Secretary of State, gives survivors of sexual assault, domestic violence, stalking, and others who fear for their safety a PO Box address and forwards their mail to their real address, so the home address stays confidential.
rules.quote: Safe at Home is a statewide address confidentiality program administered by the Office of the Minnesota Secretary of State. It is designed to help survivors of domestic violence, sexual assault, stalking, or others who fear for their safety maintain a confidential address.
rules.pinpoint: Secretary of State, Safe at Home page, program description

rules.summary: Reimbursement claims and their supporting documents and reports are investigative data while the claim is open, and private data on individuals once it is paid, denied, withdrawn, or abandoned; the board may still forward them to local law enforcement for restitution purposes.
rules.quote: Following the payment, denial, withdrawal, or abandonment of a claim, the claim and supporting documents and reports are private data on individuals as defined in section 13.02, subdivision 12

coverage.notes: Program pages on dps.mn.gov load their FAQ accordion text by script, so the saved page snapshot has only headings, phone, and history; rules lean on the statute, Minn. R. 3050.3200, the brochure, the application form, the mileage form, and the program's own October 2025 training slides. The exam statute caps state payment to the provider at $1,400 adjusted annually for inflation since January 1, 2024; that is a provider payment cap, not a survivor limit, so it is not recorded as an expense_cap. Not found: no dollar cap on medical (the board sets a payment percentage each fiscal year under Minn. R. 3050.3700 and 3050.3800); transportation is paid at the federal mileage rate with no dollar cap found; no coverage for security found (slides list security systems as not covered); the statute sets no emergency award amount; the counseling limit appears only in the training slides, not in a published fee schedule. How to file: the application form (MN-S10, Rev. 5/24, still the live version) lists the mailing address, fax, and email; the program page links the online Victim Services Portal. No in-person filing method and no processing time or decision deadline was found in the statute or program sources.

researcher_notes: Disagreement: Minn. Stat. 611A.52, subd. 8(b)(7) covers moving, storage, and phone and utility installation fees up to $1,000 per claim when a move is needed for safety, but the program's 2025 training slides (MN-S12, slide 33) list moving expenses as non-covered (the slides' non-covered list is recorded as MN-EXC-SECURITY, MN-EXC-CLOTHING, and MN-EXC-LEGAL; moving is deliberately not recorded as excluded). The statute wins per SCHEMA rule 3, so MN-CAP-RELOCATION is kept; the survivor should confirm with the board. The counseling $7,500 limit, crime scene cleanup $10,000 limit, misconduct waiver for sexual assault, and residency statement come only from the 2025 training slides, whose PDF text extraction is partly garbled; the quoted strings were checked as clean. Minn. R. 3050.3800 says the board resets counseling and medical limits each fiscal year. The slides also say evidentiary exams are not paid by the reimbursement program because the Sexual Assault Exam Payment Program pays them. The OVC directory still uses the old name, Crime Victims Reparations Board (renamed Reimbursement Board in 2023). Phones: 651-201-7300 and toll free 888-622-8799. Review pass: MN-REPORT-3 is a cooperation rule, not an alternative to the police report, so its alternatives list is empty. The counseling, cleanup, and alternative healing limits come from the slides and are treated as per claim; the slides do not say per claim or per victim. The slides also say counseling is paid at 70 percent, dental at 90 percent, and medical at 60 percent of the bill with the provider writing off the rest. The application form says the 30-day report has exceptions for child abuse and sexual assault. Packet step: MN-S10 is the current application PDF (same size as the live file, last modified March 2026); it has 53 fillable AcroForm fields. The mail, fax, and email rules quote the form's 'Complete and submit to' box. The online rule quotes the program page's link text; the URL itself is the href on that page, not printed in the snapshot text. The program page's accordion (in the raw HTML only) says the signed application may be mailed, faxed, or emailed. The Board itself obtains the police report and medical records using the signed releases, so those are not recorded as documents the survivor must include. Privacy step: Safe at Home (Minn. Stat. ch. 5B, Secretary of State) is the address confidentiality program; the SOS page (MN-S15) names sexual assault survivors, and Minn. Stat. 5B.02(e) (MN-S13) defines an eligible person to include a victim of sexual assault, with Minnesota residency or intent to reside within 60 days and excluding registered predatory offenders. The SOS page says enrollment goes through an Application Assistant; the statute (5B.03, MN-S14) says applications are filed with the secretary of state, certification lasts four years, and the secretary designates one mailing address for participants. Record confidentiality: Minn. Stat. 611A.57, subd. 6 makes claims investigative data under section 13.39 while open and private data on individuals after the claim closes, but the board may forward claim forms and reports to local law enforcement under 611A.67. Separately, Minn. Stat. 609.35(d) (MN-S5) makes sexual assault exam payment requests private data. The application form (MN-S10) also tells applicants their claim is confidential.
